hook: Babel may have been a real Babylonian tower.
facts: Genesis says that after the flood, everyone spoke one language. People decided to build a city with a tower reaching to the heavens, to make a name for themselves, using baked bricks and tar instead of stone.
In the story, God confuses their language so they can no longer understand each other, and they scatter across the earth. Genesis links the name Babel to a Hebrew word meaning to confuse.

Many historians think the story was inspired by the ziggurats of Mesopotamia, huge stepped temple towers. In Babylon stood one called Etemenanki, the temple of the foundation of heaven and earth, about ninety meters tall.

The famous painting of the tower by Pieter Bruegel the Elder makes it look like the Roman Colosseum. Today, many people say a European Parliament building in Strasbourg looks just like Bruegel's unfinished tower.

hook: For almost a thousand years, no cathedral was bigger.
facts: Hagia Sophia means holy wisdom in Greek, not Saint Sophia. It was built in Constantinople, today's Istanbul, by the emperor Justinian, and it took less than six years, finishing in the year five thirty seven.
Its giant dome seems to float on a ring of forty windows. But earthquakes were a problem, and only about twenty years after it was finished, the first dome collapsed and had to be rebuilt.
For almost a thousand years, Hagia Sophia was the largest cathedral in the world. It only lost that title in the fifteen hundreds, when the cathedral of Seville in Spain was finally completed.

In fourteen fifty three, the Ottomans conquered the city and turned Hagia Sophia into a mosque. In nineteen thirty four it became a museum, and in twenty twenty it became a mosque again, still open to visitors.

hook: Paul's name is on almost half the New Testament.
facts: Before he followed Jesus, Paul, then called Saul, persecuted Christians. The Book of Acts says he guarded the coats of the men who stoned Stephen, the first Christian martyr, and approved of his death.
Paul was a tentmaker by trade. Even while preaching, he often worked with his own hands to pay his way, so that nobody could say he was preaching for money.

Thirteen of the twenty seven books of the New Testament are letters carrying the name of Paul. Scholars debate whether he wrote all of them himself, but his letters are among the oldest Christian writings we have.

Paul wrote that he was shipwrecked three times, beaten with rods three times, and stoned once, and that was before his famous shipwreck on Malta. Tradition says he was finally beheaded in Rome under the emperor Nero.

hook: The Bible mentions giants before and after the flood.
facts: The Nephilim appear in just a few verses of Genesis, right before the story of the flood. They are called the mighty men of old, men of renown, and their name is often translated as giants.
Genesis says they appeared when the sons of God took human wives. Some ancient writers said these sons of God were fallen angels, while others think they were simply men from the family of Seth.

The Nephilim show up again after the flood. In the Book of Numbers, spies sent into Canaan say they saw them, and that next to them, we were like grasshoppers. That puzzle has fascinated readers for thousands of years.
The Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text left out of most Bibles, tells a much longer story. It says fallen angels taught humans secret arts, and their giant children brought chaos to the earth.

hook: The Book of Jonah never says it was a whale.
facts: God told Jonah to go to Nineveh, a great city of the Assyrians, Israel's enemies. Instead, Jonah boarded a ship sailing the other way, toward Tarshish, which many think was in Spain.
A terrible storm hit the ship. The sailors cast lots to find who was to blame, and the lot fell on Jonah. He told them to throw him overboard, and as soon as they did, the sea became calm.

The Hebrew text says a great fish swallowed Jonah, and he stayed inside three days and three nights. The Greek word later used by Matthew means sea monster. The whale mostly comes from old English translations.
When Jonah finally preached in Nineveh, the whole city repented, even the king. Jonah was angry that God spared them, and the book ends with God asking him a question that Jonah never answers.

hook: One church honors Pontius Pilate as a saint.
facts: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea from about the year twenty six to thirty six. Roman and Jewish writers describe him as harsh and stubborn, a man who often offended the people he ruled.
For a long time, there was no proof of Pilate outside written texts. Then in nineteen sixty one, archaeologists in Caesarea found a stone carved with his name and title, now called the Pilate Stone.

In the Gospels, Pilate washes his hands and says he is innocent of the blood of Jesus. Because of this, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church honors both Pilate and his wife as saints, believing he later became a Christian.

Matthew says that during the trial, Pilate's wife sent him an urgent message. She had suffered much in a dream because of Jesus, and she warned her husband to have nothing to do with that righteous man.

hook: Early Christians did not hide in the catacombs.
facts: Under Rome lie dozens of catacombs, underground tunnels dug into soft volcanic rock. Together they stretch for well over one hundred kilometers, on several levels, some more than twenty meters deep.
Their walls are lined with shelves cut into the rock, where bodies were wrapped in cloth and sealed in. Hundreds of thousands of people may have been buried there, many of them poor Christians.

Movies show Christians hiding in the catacombs from Roman persecution, but historians say they were mainly cemeteries. Roman law protected burial places, and Christians went there to bury and remember their dead, not to live in secret.

The catacombs hold some of the oldest Christian art in the world. Early believers painted the Good Shepherd, Jonah and the whale, and the fish symbol on their walls, long before the first big churches.

hook: King Solomon had seven hundred wives.
facts: When Solomon became king, the Bible says God offered him anything he wanted. Instead of riches or a long life, he asked for wisdom to rule well, and God was so pleased that he gave him riches and honor too.
Solomon built the first Temple in Jerusalem. The Bible says no hammer, axe or iron tool was heard at the site, because the stones were cut and prepared at the quarry before being brought there.

The First Book of Kings says Solomon had seven hundred wives who were princesses, and three hundred concubines. Many were foreign brides that sealed alliances, and the Bible says they turned his heart to other gods.

The Bible says Solomon spoke three thousand proverbs, wrote more than a thousand songs, and could teach about trees, animals, birds and fish. Tradition links him to Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and the Song of Songs.

hook: Methuselah died in the year of the flood.
facts: Methuselah is the oldest person in the Bible. Genesis says he lived nine hundred and sixty nine years, which is why people still say as old as Methuselah about something extremely old.
Methuselah came from a remarkable family. His father was Enoch, who walked with God and then was no more, because God took him. And his grandson was Noah, the builder of the ark.
If you add up the ages given in Genesis, Methuselah died in the very same year the great flood began. Some Jewish traditions even say the flood was delayed seven days so he could be mourned.

A bristlecone pine in the White Mountains of California is nicknamed Methuselah. It is more than four thousand eight hundred years old, one of the oldest known trees, and its exact location is kept secret.

hook: The Sea of Galilee is actually a lake.
facts: Many of the most famous Gospel stories happen around this lake. It is where Jesus called fishermen like Peter and Andrew, calmed a storm, and, according to the Gospels, walked on the water.

In nineteen eighty six, during a drought, two brothers found an ancient fishing boat in the mud of the shore. It dates from around the time of Jesus, and it is now shown in a museum as the Jesus Boat.
Despite its name, the Sea of Galilee is a freshwater lake, only about twenty one kilometers long. It lies about two hundred meters below sea level, making it the lowest freshwater lake on Earth.
Its sudden storms are real. Cool winds rush down from the hills into the low basin, and the calm water can turn into dangerous waves in minutes, just like in the Gospel stories.

hook: Joan of Arc was only nineteen when she died.
facts: Joan was a peasant girl from a village in eastern France. At about thirteen, she said she began hearing the voices of saints, who later told her to help the French king during the Hundred Years War.

At seventeen, Joan convinced the future King Charles the Seventh to give her armor and send her with an army to Orleans. The city had been under siege for months, and she helped free it in just nine days.

Joan was captured, tried by a church court backed by the English, and burned at the stake in Rouen in fourteen thirty one. She was only nineteen. Twenty five years later, a new trial declared her innocent.
Almost five hundred years after her death, in nineteen twenty, the Catholic Church declared Joan of Arc a saint. Today she is one of the patron saints of France.

hook: One Bible still includes the Book of Enoch.
facts: The Book of Enoch is an ancient Jewish text named after Enoch, the great grandfather of Noah. Parts of it are more than two thousand years old, and it was popular among Jews and early Christians.
The Letter of Jude, in the New Testament, actually quotes the Book of Enoch, about the Lord coming with thousands of his holy ones. Yet most churches later decided to leave Enoch out of their Bible.

For centuries, the full book was lost in Europe. But the Ethiopian Orthodox Church kept it in its Bible all along, and in the seventeen hundreds, the Scottish explorer James Bruce brought copies back from Ethiopia.

Enoch describes fallen angels called Watchers, who came down to earth and taught humans secrets like metalworking and makeup. Their children were giants, and the book says their evil led to the great flood.

hook: According to the Bible, Elijah never died.
facts: During a long drought, Elijah hid by a brook, and the Bible says ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and evening. Later, a poor widow shared her last flour with him, and her jar never ran empty.

On Mount Carmel, Elijah challenged four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal to see whose god would send fire. Baal's prophets shouted all day, while Elijah even soaked his altar with water before praying.
Elijah did not die like everyone else. The Second Book of Kings says a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared, and he was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind while his disciple Elisha watched.
Because he never died, Jewish tradition expects Elijah to return one day. At the Passover meal, many families pour a cup of wine for him and open the door, in case Elijah comes in.

hook: Several churches claim to have the Holy Grail.
facts: The Holy Grail is said to be the cup Jesus used at the Last Supper. The Gospels mention the cup but never say what happened to it, and the Grail legend only appeared more than eleven hundred years later.

The first known Grail story was written in France around eleven ninety by the poet Chretien de Troyes. Surprisingly, his grail was not the cup of Jesus at all, just a mysterious dish carried through a castle.
The most famous claim is in Valencia Cathedral in Spain, an ancient agate cup that popes have even used to celebrate Mass. In Leon, also in Spain, a basilica displays another candidate.

In later legends, Joseph of Arimathea used the Grail to catch the blood of Jesus at the cross, then carried it to Britain. That is how the Grail became part of the stories of King Arthur and his knights.

hook: Peter asked to be crucified upside down.
facts: Peter's real name was Simon. Jesus gave him a new name, Cephas in Aramaic and Petros in Greek, both meaning rock. That is why Jesus says, on this rock I will build my church.
Peter was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee, working with his brother Andrew. He was also married, because the Gospels say Jesus healed his mother in law, who was sick with a fever.

Christian tradition says Peter was crucified in Rome under the emperor Nero. Feeling unworthy to die like Jesus, he asked to be crucified upside down. Saint Peter's Basilica stands over his traditional grave.
On the night Jesus was arrested, Peter denied knowing him three times before the rooster crowed. Later the risen Jesus asked him three times, do you love me, as if to undo each denial.

hook: Jericho may be the oldest walled city on Earth.
facts: According to the Book of Joshua, the Israelites did not attack Jericho at first. They marched around the city once a day for six days, with priests blowing trumpets made of rams' horns.
On the seventh day, they marched around the city seven times. Then the priests blew the trumpets, the people gave a great shout, and the Bible says the walls of Jericho fell down flat.

Jericho is one of the oldest cities in the world. Archaeologists found a stone wall and a stone tower there more than ten thousand years old, built before writing, before metal tools, even before pottery.
Before the attack, a woman named Rahab hid two Israelite spies on her roof under stalks of flax. She tied a scarlet cord in her window as a sign, and her family was spared when the city fell.

hook: Construction started in eighteen eighty two, and continues today.
facts: The Sagrada Familia is a basilica in Barcelona, Spain, designed by the architect Antoni Gaudi. He took over the project in eighteen eighty three and spent the rest of his life working on it.
Gaudi was inspired by nature. Inside, the columns branch out like trees, so visitors feel they are standing in a stone forest, with colored light pouring in through the stained glass windows.
Building began in eighteen eighty two, and it is still not completely finished. When people asked why it was taking so long, Gaudi reportedly answered, my client is not in a hurry, meaning God.
In nineteen twenty six, Gaudi was hit by a tram in Barcelona. Dressed so simply, he was mistaken for a beggar and not treated quickly. He died days later and is buried inside his basilica.

hook: Goliath's height depends on which Bible you read.
facts: Goliath was the champion of the Philistines, from the city of Gath. For forty days, morning and evening, he came out and challenged the army of Israel to send one man to fight him.
His armor was enormous. The Bible says his bronze coat weighed five thousand shekels, about fifty seven kilograms, and the iron tip of his spear alone weighed around seven kilograms.

Most Bibles say Goliath was six cubits and a span, nearly three meters tall. But the oldest Greek translation and a Dead Sea Scroll say four cubits and a span, about two meters. Very tall, but not a monster.
David refused King Saul's armor because he was not used to it. He went out with only his staff, a sling and five smooth stones from a stream. He needed just one.

hook: Gabriel made a priest mute for doubting him.
facts: Gabriel is one of only a few angels named in the Bible. He first appears in the Book of Daniel, explaining Daniel's visions, and his name is often translated as God is my strength.
Gabriel is best known for the Annunciation. In the Gospel of Luke, he visits Mary in Nazareth and tells her she will give birth to a son, who will be called the Son of God.

Before visiting Mary, Gabriel appeared to an old priest named Zechariah to announce the birth of his son, John the Baptist. Zechariah doubted it, so Gabriel made him unable to speak until the baby was born.
Gabriel is important in Islam too. Muslims believe the angel Gabriel, Jibril in Arabic, revealed the Quran to the Prophet Muhammad. So the same angel is honored by Jews, Christians and Muslims.

hook: Daniel served kings of two different empires.
facts: Daniel was taken from Jerusalem to Babylon as a young man. He and his friends refused the king's rich food and wine and ate only vegetables and water, yet after ten days they looked healthier than everyone else.
King Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a huge statue with a head of gold, a chest of silver, a belly of bronze, and feet of iron mixed with clay. Only Daniel could explain what it meant.

Daniel served the kings of Babylon, then kept serving when the Persians took over, under Darius and Cyrus. That is why he was still a top official when jealous rivals tricked the king into throwing him to the lions.
In the city of Susa, in modern Iran, a building with a cone shaped dome is visited as the tomb of Daniel. Other places also claim his grave, but this one has been honored for many centuries.
